newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin op possible from next week - U.S. surgeon.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin op possible from next week - U.S. surgeon.

text.p: Doctors have dealt with anaemia and thyroid problems to get President Boris Yeltsin ready for heart surgery which could go ahead next week, a Russian newspaper on Friday quoted U.S. surgeon Michael DeBakey as saying.
DeBakey, who will be a consultant during the bypass operation, told the Moskovsky Komsomolets newspaper that Yeltsin was "in fine form".
"The operation can take place at any time, starting from next week. Doctors have successfully managed to cope with serious anaemia and a disfunctional thyroid gland," he said.
"I do not know the exact date of the operation yet. But I can say that Mr Yeltsin has been well prepared for it."

DeBakey, who carried out the world's first successful heart bypass operation, is due to meet Yeltsin's doctors in Moscow on Monday. He said he would stay in Russia as long as he was needed but that he would not operate himself.
Russian surgeon Renat Akchurin, who is expected to lead the operating team, was a "first-class specialist", he said.

Akchurin visited DeBakey's Houston clinic last month and returned with equipment which could be used during the operation. DeBakey said the machinery would stay in Russia after Yeltsin's operation for use with other patients.
Yeltsin, 65, said on September 5 he had agreed to have the operation to improve the supply of blood to his heart.
Doctors said on September 25 that it would take six to 10 weeks to get the president ready for surgery. The six-week period ends next week.
